text.p: Investment houses Salomon Bros and SBC Warburg have recommended shares of Portugal's Portucel Industrial because of promising conditions in the pulp sector and expectations that the firm will return to profits in 1997.

"Portucel has one of the lowest production costs in the European pulp industry, and we believe the company, even at current depressed pulp prices, will produce a profit for 1997," Salomon said in a May report.
Warburg forecast that improving demand, supply and inventory balances would help pulp prices recover and boost Portucel's earnings.
"Given that the sector can move quickly and sharply, we believe investors should buy the sector over the next six months," it said in a May report.
Warburg made its recommendation on May 9 when Portucel shares stood at 1,241 escudos and Salomon made its recommendation on May 19 when the share price exceeded 1,200 escudos.
Portucel shares stood at 1,209 escudos, up 30, in volume of 218,012 on Lisbon bourse at 1442 GMT.
